target: def Target (𝓑 : S₀) (K : Fm → Fm) : Prop := ∀ φ, 𝓑 ⊢ φ → 𝓑 ⊢ K φ
a_raw: {"translation":"For any sentence type Fm and system type S₀ with a provability relation on Fm, any system 𝓑 of type S₀, and any function K from Fm to Fm, Target(𝓑, K) is defined to mean: for every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ, then 𝓑 proves K(φ). This is a meta-level implication between provability claims, not a requirement that 𝓑 prove the sentence φ 🡒 K(φ). It imposes no condition on K(φ) when 𝓑 does not prove φ, and requires neither classicality nor consistency of 𝓑."}
translation: For any sentence type Fm and system type S₀ with a provability relation on Fm, any system 𝓑 of type S₀, and any function K from Fm to Fm, Target(𝓑, K) is defined to mean: for every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ, then 𝓑 proves K(φ). This is a meta-level implication between provability claims, not a requirement that 𝓑 prove the sentence φ 🡒 K(φ). It imposes no condition on K(φ) when 𝓑 does not prove φ, and requires neither classicality nor consistency of 𝓑.

judgement.summary: With 𝓑 interpreted as EA, `Target` states exactly the derived rule: whenever EA proves φ, EA also proves Kφ. This is a meta-level condition on the base theory alone, not an object-language axiom φ → Kφ or a closure requirement on an extension.
